chunks: And ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a menstruating woman who performs ghusl while saffron remains on her body and the water does not remove it. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

And about a woman who performs ghusl after combing with hair extensions, and she does not undo her hair: how much water is sufficient for her? He عليه السلام said: “The amount that her hair absorbs; and that is three handfuls over her head, two handfuls on the right, and two handfuls on the left. Then she passes her hand over all of her body.”

key_terms.بِقَرَامِلَ: with hair extensions or attached hair strands used in combing
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is unobjectionable

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl valid if saffron remains on the body or if a woman does not undo her hair?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning ghusl for women. It states that leftover saffron on the body does not invalidate ghusl, and that a woman with bound or arranged hair does not need to undo it if enough water reaches it and she washes her whole body in the described manner.
